Defining cohorts

Source: vignettes/articles/cohorts.Rmd
cohorts.Rmd

Flag diagnoses and procedures

The analyst supplies literal code prefixes. Each slot is tested separately; punctuation, spaces, and case in the supplied prefixes are normalized.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  nis_flag_dx(principal_hf = "I50", position = "principal") |>
  nis_flag_pr(ablation = "02L")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis |> dplyr::count(heart_failure, principal_hf, ablation) |> dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   heart_failure principal_hf ablation     n
#>   <lgl>         <lgl>        <lgl>    <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE         FALSE        FALSE       36
#> 2 TRUE          TRUE         FALSE      108
#> 3 FALSE         FALSE        TRUE        48

The table shows synthetic discharge counts for each flag combination. To make a principal-only diagnosis flag, call nis_flag_dx() with position = "principal"; use "secondary" for slots after the principal one. nis_flag_pr() supports "any" and "principal".

Supply several named definitions in one call when they share the same position and system. For example, use nis_flag_dx(nis, heart_failure = "I50", hypertension = "I10") to add both flags to the same DuckDB projection.

Classify diagnoses and procedures with CCSR

nis_add_ccsr() matches complete ICD-10 codes to the bundled AHRQ mappings in DuckDB. An any-slot search returns a list of distinct categories for each discharge. Supply categories to keep only the categories relevant to the study. For a mutually exclusive grouping by principal diagnosis, use position = "default" to return the inpatient default category.

nis |>
  nis_add_ccsr(categories = "CIR019", name = "hf_categories") |>
  nis_add_ccsr(position = "default", name = "principal_ccsr") |>
  dplyr::filter(length(hf_categories) > 0L) |>
  dplyr::count(principal_ccsr) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   principal_ccsr     n
#>   <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 CIR019           108

Use type = "pr" for procedures. The default release selection covers Q4 2015 and calendar years 2016–2024 with the bundled v2025.1. ICD-9 and years outside the bundled coverage yield missing results. Pin version = "2025.1" to use the same definitions across years and to include Q1–Q3 2025 if DQTR is present. Report the CCSR version in the study methods. Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project. Clinical Classifications Software Refined (CCSR), v2025.1, November 2024.

Add procedure timing

Procedure timing compares matching procedure slots with the corresponding PRDAY fields. This small invented data frame makes the slot relationship visible.

toy <- data.frame(
  I10_PR1 = c("02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ"),
  I10_PR2 = c("0JH604Z", "0JH604Z", "0JH604Z"),
  PRDAY1 = c(0L, 2L, 0L), PRDAY2 = c(1L, 1L, NA_integer_)
)
nis_flag_pr_timing(toy, "02UG0", "0JH60", relation = "after")
#>   I10_PR1 I10_PR2 PRDAY1 PRDAY2 outcome_post_index
#> 1 02UG0JZ 0JH604Z      0      1               TRUE
#> 2 02UG0JZ 0JH604Z      2      1              FALSE
#> 3 02UG0JZ 0JH604Z      0     NA              FALSE

The flag is true when an outcome procedure is documented after the earliest index procedure. Missing or sentinel days need an explicit missing_day policy. nis_audit_prday() summarizes how often matching slots have a known day.

Count cohort steps

Define the eligibility rules once in nis_attrition(). With .design = TRUE, the baseline includes discharges with valid survey design fields. Missing criterion values exclude discharges at that step. Inject the combined rule with !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow) to use the same eligibility criteria in nis_design().

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
flow <- nis_attrition(
  nis, adults = AGE >= 18, heart_failure = heart_failure, .design = TRUE
)
flow
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>    step criterion               n_unweighted n_dropped_unweighted n_weighted
#>   <int> <chr>                          <int>                <int>      <dbl>
#> 1     0 Valid design discharges           96                   NA      114. 
#> 2     1 adults                            96                    0      114. 
#> 3     2 heart_failure                     54                   42       62.4
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_dropped_weighted <dbl>, pct_retained <dbl>

design <- nis_design(nis, cohort = !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow), keep = LOS)
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
dplyr::summarise(design, discharges = srvyr::unweighted(dplyr::n()))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   discharges
#>        <int>
#> 1         54

Pass the same input to both calls so the last unweighted attrition count is the survey domain denominator. The design retains the sampling structure of hospital-years with zero eligible discharges. Leave .design at its default when the attrition table should start with every discharge in the input. For alternate diagnosis positions and changes over time, see Code transitions and sensitivity.

Record eligibility across the 2015 transition

Supply named code criteria in .codes to use the same definitions for eligibility and the transition audit. The code criteria run in list order after the logical criteria in .... Here the first code step finds a match in any diagnosis slot and the second requires a principal match. These definitions illustrate the workflow on invented data.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2015))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Experimental: years before 2016 store ICD-9-CM codes in DX1, PR1, ... slots.
#> ℹ Flag them with `system = "icd9"`; 2015 mixes ICD-9 (Q1-Q3) and ICD-10 (Q4)
#>   slots.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
prefixes <- list(icd9 = c("123", "12345", "V0001"), icd10 = c("I50", "Z515"))
flow <- nis_attrition(
  nis,
  adults = AGE >= 18,
  .codes = list(
    matching_dx = list(type = "dx", system = "both", position = "any", codes = prefixes),
    principal_dx = list(type = "dx", system = "both", position = "principal", codes = prefixes)
  ),
  .design = TRUE
)
flow
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>    step criterion               n_unweighted n_dropped_unweighted n_weighted
#>   <int> <chr>                          <int>                <int>      <dbl>
#> 1     0 Valid design discharges           96                   NA      114. 
#> 2     1 adults                            96                    0      114. 
#> 3     2 matching_dx                       91                    5      108. 
#> 4     3 principal_dx                      54                   37       62.4
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_dropped_weighted <dbl>, pct_retained <dbl>
attr(flow, "nis_criteria")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   criterion    type  position  system codes           
#>   <chr>        <chr> <chr>     <chr>  <list>          
#> 1 adults       NA    NA        NA     <NULL>          
#> 2 matching_dx  dx    any       both   <named list [2]>
#> 3 principal_dx dx    principal both   <named list [2]>

design <- nis_design(nis, cohort = !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow), keep = c(AGE, LOS))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ AGE, design = design)
stats::nobs(fit)
#> [1] 54

The criteria table records the system and slot rule for Methods. Here the last attrition count equals the number of observations in the model because AGE and LOS are complete among eligible discharges. See the quarterly audit of these criteria.

Save a cohort for another session

Pass the full lazy sample and the eligibility rule to nis_write_cohort(). Keep the columns you expect to use in later analyses. The writer creates a new directory with yearly Parquet parts and saves the eligibility expression, source years, and easyNIS version in each part’s metadata.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
path <- nis_write_cohort(nis, heart_failure & AGE >= 50, tempfile(),
                         keep = c(AGE, LOS))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

# In a later session
design <- nis_design(nis_open(path), keep = c(AGE, LOS), annualize = TRUE)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmplz7zan/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
design |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 65) |>
  dplyr::summarise(discharges = srvyr::survey_total())
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   discharges discharges_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1       25.2          3.57

The saved cohort carries one placeholder per sampled hospital-year with no eligible discharge. This preserves the survey variance structure, including whole strata and years where the cohort is empty. Annualization still uses all years with valid design records. Keep the original design run if you need its invalid-design exclusion counts or full-sample quarter coverage.

Apply additional patient filters to the survey design after reopening. When inspecting raw Parquet rows, use dplyr::filter(.in_cohort) before counting discharges. To re-save a cohort with fewer columns, pass its reopened query to nis_write_cohort() and omit cohort. To change the eligibility rule, return to the source sample.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • A prefix is not a validated clinical code set. Define, document, and review it for the study question.
  • A cross-year definition may span different code systems. Do not assume code counts are comparable across the 2015 transition.
  • Unknown procedure days are not equivalent to day zero; choose and report a missing-day policy.

Reference pages: nis_flag_dx(), nis_flag_pr(), nis_flag_pr_timing(), nis_attrition(), nis_audit_prday().
